doc: /-- Each Gauss term is bounded by the Gauss norm. -/

statement:
theorem exists_norm_eq_norm_coeff_mul_prod (f : Restricted R c) :
    ∃ t : σ →₀ ℕ, ‖f‖ = ‖coeff t f.1‖ * t.prod (c · ^ ·)

well-defined"). -/

theorem exists_norm_coeff_eq (f : Restricted R (1 : σ → ℝ)) :
    ∃ t : σ →₀ ℕ, ‖coeff t f.1‖ = ‖f‖

name: reduction_eq_zero_iff
statement:
theorem reduction_eq_zero_iff (f : unitClosedBall (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))) :
    reduction f = 0 ↔ ‖(f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))‖ < 1
doc:
/-- The reduction vanishes exactly on the series of Gauss norm less than one. Source: BGR 5.1.2
("Obviously the kernel of this map is `Tₙˇ`"); Bosch 1.2 ("`f̃ = 0` if and only if `|f| < 1`"). -/

name: norm_eq_one_of_reduction_ne_zero

theorem norm_eq_one_of_reduction_ne_zero {f : unitClosedBall (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))}

name: ker_reduction

    RingHom.ker (reduction (K := K) (σ := σ)) = openUnitBallIdeal (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))

name: norm_toRestricted_map_subtype_le_one
statement:
theorem norm_toRestricted_map_subtype_le_one (p : MvPolynomial σ (unitClosedBall K)) :

name: reduction_ofUnitBallPolynomial
statement:
theorem reduction_ofUnitBallPolynomial (p : MvPolynomial σ (unitClosedBall K)) :
    reduction (ofUnitBallPolynomial p) = MvPolynomial.map (residue (unitClosedBall K)) p

name: exists_sub_ofUnitBallPolynomial_mem_openUnitBallIdeal

theorem exists_sub_ofUnitBallPolynomial_mem_openUnitBallIdeal

/-- Every series of the unit ball is a polynomial over the unit ball of `K` up to a series of Gauss
norm less than one. -/

name: reduction_surjective

name: reductionEquiv_mk

name: isPowerBounded_iff_forall_norm_coeff_le_one
statement:
theorem isPowerBounded_iff_forall_norm_coeff_le_one {f : Restricted 𝕜 (1 : σ → ℝ)} :
    PowerBounded.IsPowerBounded f ↔ ∀ t, ‖coeff t f.1‖ ≤ 1

/-- The power-bounded elements of the Tate algebra are the series with coefficients in the unit
ball. Source: BGR 5.1.2 ("`T̊ₙ = Tₙ°`"). -/

name: isTopologicallyNilpotent_iff_forall_norm_coeff_lt_one
statement:
theorem isTopologicallyNilpotent_iff_forall_norm_coeff_lt_one {f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)} :
    IsTopologicallyNilpotent f ↔ ∀ t, ‖coeff t f.1‖ < 1
doc:
/-- The topologically nilpotent elements of the Tate algebra are the series with coefficients in
the open unit ball. Source: BGR 5.1.2 ("`Ťₙ = Tₙˇ`"). -/

name: isUnit_iff_norm_coeff_lt
statement:
theorem isUnit_iff_norm_coeff_lt {f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)} :
    IsUnit f ↔ coeff 0 f.1 ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ t ≠ 0, ‖coeff t f.1‖ < ‖coeff 0 f.1‖
doc:
/-- **The units of the Tate algebra**: a series is a unit if and only if its constant coefficient
strictly dominates every other coefficient. Source: BGR 5.1.3/1; Bosch 1.2/4. -/

name: isUnit_iff_isUnit_reduction
statement:
theorem isUnit_iff_isUnit_reduction (f : unitClosedBall (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))) :
    IsUnit f ↔ IsUnit (reduction f)
doc:
/-- An element of the unit ball of the Tate algebra is a unit there if and only if its reduction
is a unit. Source: BGR 5.1.3/1. -/

name: isUnit_coe_iff_isUnit_reduction
doc:
/-- A series of Gauss norm one is a unit of the Tate algebra if and only if its reduction is a
unit. Source: BGR 5.1.3/1 ("`f` is a unit if and only if `f̃` is a unit in `T̃ₙ`"). -/

name: exists_norm_eq_one_not_isUnit_C_add
statement:
theorem exists_norm_eq_one_not_isUnit_C_add {f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)} (hf : ‖f‖ = 1) :
    ∃ a : K, ‖a‖ = 1 ∧ ¬ IsUnit (C (1 : σ → ℝ) a + f)
doc:
/-- For a series of Gauss norm one there is a constant of norm one whose sum with it is not a
unit. Source: BGR 5.1.3/2. -/

statement: theorem jacobson_bot : Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))) = ⊥
doc:
/-- **The Jacobson radical of the Tate algebra is zero**: the intersection of all maximal ideals
is `0`. Source: BGR 5.1.3/3. -/

name: norm_map_mul_prod_pow_le
statement:
theorem norm_map_mul_prod_pow_le (hφ : ∀ r, ‖φ r‖ ≤ ‖r‖) (hx : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ c i) (a : R)
    (t : σ →₀ ℕ) : ‖φ a * t.prod fun i k ↦ x i ^ k‖ ≤ ‖a‖ * t.prod (c · ^ ·)

name: tendsto_map_coeff_mul_prod_pow

    Tendsto (fun t : σ →₀ ℕ ↦ φ (coeff t f.1) * t.prod fun i k ↦ x i ^ k) cofinite (𝓝 0)

    Summable fun t : σ →₀ ℕ ↦ φ (coeff t f.1) * t.prod fun i k ↦ x i ^ k

/-- The evaluated series converges. Source: BGR 5.1.4 ("Since `a_ν x^ν` is a zero-sequence in `L`,

    aeval c x hx (MvPolynomial.toRestricted c p) = MvPolynomial.aeval x p
doc: /-- On polynomials, evaluation is polynomial evaluation. -/

name: norm_aeval_le
statement: theorem norm_aeval_le (f : Restricted K c) : ‖aeval c x hx f‖ ≤ ‖f‖

theorem algHom_ext_of_continuous {ψ₁ ψ₂ : Restricted K c →ₐ[K] B} (h₁ : Continuous ψ₁)

name: (anonymous)
statement: instance : IsLocalHom (unitClosedBallMap K L)

name: norm_aeval_le_one
statement:
theorem norm_aeval_le_one {B : Type*} [NormedCommRing B] [NormedAlgebra K B] [NormOneClass B]
    [IsUltrametricDist B] [CompleteSpace B] {x : σ → B} (hx : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ 1)
    (f : unitClosedBall (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))) :
    ‖aeval (1 : σ → ℝ) x hx (f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))‖ ≤ 1
doc:
/-- Evaluation at a tuple of the unit ball maps the unit ball of the Tate algebra to the unit
ball. Source: BGR 5.1.4/2. -/

name: residue_aeval
statement:
theorem residue_aeval {x : σ → L} (hx : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ 1)
    (f : unitClosedBall (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))) :
    residue (unitClosedBall L)
        ⟨aeval (1 : σ → ℝ) x hx (f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)),
          mem_unitClosedBall.2 (norm_aeval_le_one hx f)⟩ =
      MvPolynomial.eval₂ (NormedField.residueFieldMap K L)
        (fun i ↦ residue (unitClosedBall L) ⟨x i, mem_unitClosedBall.2 (hx i)⟩) (reduction f)
doc:
/-- **Reduction commutes with evaluation at a point**: for a point `x` of the unit ball of a
complete extension field `L`, the residue class of `f(x)` is the value of the reduced polynomial
`f̃` at the reduced point `x̃`. Source: BGR 5.1.4 (the commutative diagram before Proposition 3);
Bosch 1.2/5. -/

name: reduction_aeval
statement:
theorem reduction_aeval {x : σ → Restricted K (1 : τ → ℝ)} (hx : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ 1)
    (f : unitClosedBall (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))) :
    reduction ⟨aeval (1 : σ → ℝ) x hx (f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)),
        mem_unitClosedBall.2 (norm_aeval_le_one hx f)⟩ =
      MvPolynomial.aeval (fun i ↦ reduction ⟨x i, mem_unitClosedBall.2 (hx i)⟩) (reduction f)
doc:
/-- **Reduction commutes with substitution**: for a tuple `x` of the unit ball of a Tate algebra,
the reduction of `f(x)` is the reduced polynomial `f̃` evaluated at the reductions of the `x i`.
Source: BGR 5.1.3/7 (the induced `k̃`-algebra homomorphism `φ̃`), 5.2.4/1 ("`(σ(f))~ = σ̃(f̃)`"). -/

name: evalNorm_nonneg
statement: theorem evalNorm_nonneg (x : MaximalSpectrum A) (f : A) : 0 ≤ evalNorm K x f

name: evalNorm_eq_zero_of_mem
statement:
theorem evalNorm_eq_zero_of_mem {x : MaximalSpectrum A} {f : A} (hf : f ∈ x.asIdeal) :
    evalNorm K x f = 0
doc: /-- A function vanishes at the points of its zero set: `|f(x)| = 0` when `f ∈ x`. -/

name: isMaximal_ker_of_isAlgebraic
statement: theorem isMaximal_ker_of_isAlgebraic (φ : A →ₐ[K] L) : (RingHom.ker φ).IsMaximal
doc:
/-- The kernel of a `K`-algebra homomorphism into an algebraic extension field of `K` is a maximal
ideal. Source: BGR 5.1.4/6 ("`𝔪_x := ker h_x` is a `k`-algebraic maximal ideal"). -/

name: finite_quotient_ker
statement:
theorem finite_quotient_ker [FiniteDimensional K L] (φ : A →ₐ[K] L) :
    Module.Finite K (A ⧸ RingHom.ker φ)
doc:
/-- The residue field at the kernel of a `K`-algebra homomorphism into a finite extension of `K`
is finite over `K`. -/

name: evalNorm_eq_norm_algHom
statement:
theorem evalNorm_eq_norm_algHom (φ : A →ₐ[K] L) (x : MaximalSpectrum A)
    (hx : x.asIdeal = RingHom.ker φ) (f : A) : evalNorm K x f = ‖φ f‖
doc:
/-- At the kernel of a `K`-algebra homomorphism `φ` into an algebraic normed extension field `L`
of `K`, the value `|f(x)|` is the norm of `φ f`. Source: BGR 5.1.4/6 ("Corresponding elements in
`Tₙ/𝔪_x` and `L` must have the same spectral norm over `k`"). -/

name: evalNorm_le_norm
statement: theorem evalNorm_le_norm (x : MaximalSpectrum A) (f : A) : evalNorm K x f ≤ ‖f‖
doc:
/-- In a Banach algebra over `K` the value of a function at a point is bounded by its norm:
`|f(x)| ≤ ‖f‖`. Source: BGR 3.8.2/1; Bosch 1.2/12 (the contraction argument through units). -/

name: bddAbove_range_evalNorm
statement:
theorem bddAbove_range_evalNorm (f : A) :
    BddAbove (Set.range fun x : MaximalSpectrum A ↦ evalNorm K x f)

name: supSeminorm_le_norm
statement: theorem supSeminorm_le_norm (f : A) : supSeminorm K f ≤ ‖f‖
doc:
/-- In a Banach algebra over `K` the supremum seminorm is bounded by the norm.
Source: BGR 3.8.2/2. -/

name: NormedField.exists_lt_natCast_norm_eq_one
statement:
theorem NormedField.exists_lt_natCast_norm_eq_one (K : Type*) [NormedField K]
    [IsUltrametricDist K] (d : ℕ) : ∃ m : ℕ, d < m ∧ ‖(m : K)‖ = 1
doc: /-- In a nonarchimedean normed field there are natural numbers of norm one beyond any bound. -/

name: exists_finset_splittingField_X_pow_sub_one
statement:
theorem exists_finset_splittingField_X_pow_sub_one {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hmK : ‖(m : K)‖ = 1) :
    ∃ S : Finset (X ^ m - 1 : K[X]).SplittingField, S.card = m ∧
      (∀ s ∈ S, spectralNorm K _ s = 1) ∧
        ∀ s ∈ S, ∀ t ∈ S, s ≠ t → spectralNorm K _ (s - t) = 1
doc:
/-- The `m`-th roots of unity in the splitting field of `X ^ m - 1`, for `m` of norm one in `K`:
`m` elements of spectral norm one whose pairwise differences have spectral norm one. This is the
finite extension with a large residue field used in the maximum modulus principle; it replaces
the algebraic closure and BGR's Lemma 3.4.1/4. Source: BGR 5.1.4/3 ("These assertions remain
valid if `k_a` is replaced by any field extension `L ⊂ k_a` of `k`, provided `L̃` is infinite"). -/

name: exists_norm_aeval_eq_norm
statement:
theorem exists_norm_aeval_eq_norm (S : Finset L) (hS₁ : ∀ s ∈ S, ‖s‖ ≤ 1)
    (hS : ∀ s ∈ S, ∀ t ∈ S, s ≠ t → ‖s - t‖ = 1) (f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))
    (hf : ∀ t : σ →₀ ℕ, ‖coeff t f.1‖ = ‖f‖ → ∀ i, t i < S.card) :
    ∃ x : σ → L, ∃ hx : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ 1, (∀ i, x i ∈ S) ∧ ‖aeval (1 : σ → ℝ) x hx f‖ = ‖f‖
doc:
/-- **Maximum modulus principle at the points of an extension field.** Let `L` be a complete
extension field of `K` and `S` a finite subset of its unit ball whose elements are pairwise at
distance one, with more elements than every exponent occurring at a coefficient of `f` of maximal
norm. Then `|f(x)| = |f|` for some point `x` with coordinates in `S`. Source: BGR 5.1.4/3;
Bosch 1.2/5. -/

name: exists_evalNorm_eq_norm
statement:
theorem exists_evalNorm_eq_norm (f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)) :
    ∃ x : MaximalSpectrum (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)),
      Module.Finite K (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ) ⧸ x.asIdeal) ∧ evalNorm K x f = ‖f‖
doc:
/-- **Maximum modulus principle for the Tate algebra**: every `f` attains its Gauss norm at a
maximal ideal whose residue field is finite over `K`. Source: BGR 5.1.4/6. -/

name: exists_evalNorm_eq_norm_and_notMem
statement:
theorem exists_evalNorm_eq_norm_and_notMem (f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ))
    {g : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    ∃ x : MaximalSpectrum (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)), evalNorm K x f = ‖f‖ ∧ g ∉ x.asIdeal
doc:
/-- The points at which `f` attains its Gauss norm are Zariski-dense: every nonzero `g` is nonzero
at one of them. Source: BGR 5.1.4/4 (the product trick). -/

name: supSeminorm_eq_norm
statement: theorem supSeminorm_eq_norm (f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)) : supSeminorm K f = ‖f‖
doc: /-- **The Gauss norm is the supremum norm** on the Tate algebra. Source: BGR 5.1.4/6. -/

name: eq_zero_of_forall_mem
statement:
theorem eq_zero_of_forall_mem {f : Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)}
    (hf : ∀ x : MaximalSpectrum (Restricted K (1 : σ → ℝ)), f ∈ x.asIdeal) : f = 0
doc: /-- A series vanishing at every maximal ideal is zero. Source: BGR 5.1.4/5 (identity theorem). -/

name: coeffX0_add
statement:
theorem coeffX0_add (g h : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) (ν : ℕ) :
    coeffX0 (g + h) ν = coeffX0 g ν + coeffX0 h ν

name: coeffX0_smul
statement:
theorem coeffX0_smul (a : K) (g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) (ν : ℕ) :
    coeffX0 (a • g) ν = a • coeffX0 g ν

name: norm_coeffX0_le
statement: theorem norm_coeffX0_le (g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) (ν : ℕ) : ‖coeffX0 g ν‖ ≤ ‖g‖

name: norm_le_iff_forall_norm_coeffX0_le
statement:
theorem norm_le_iff_forall_norm_coeffX0_le {ε : ℝ} (g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) :
    ‖g‖ ≤ ε ↔ ∀ ν, ‖coeffX0 g ν‖ ≤ ε
doc: /-- The Gauss norm of `g = Σ g_ν X 0 ^ ν` is the maximum of the Gauss norms of the `g_ν`. -/

name: tendsto_norm_coeffX0
statement:
theorem tendsto_norm_coeffX0 (g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) :
    Tendsto (fun ν ↦ ‖coeffX0 g ν‖) atTop (𝓝 0)
doc:
/-- The coefficients in `X 0` of a series of the Tate algebra tend to zero. Source: BGR 5.1.1
("`Tₙ(k) = Tₙ₋₁(k)⟨Xₙ⟩`"). -/

name: ofTail_injective
statement: theorem ofTail_injective : Function.Injective (ofTail K n)

name: ofPolynomial_X
statement: theorem ofPolynomial_X : ofPolynomial K n Polynomial.X = Restricted.X K (1 : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) 0

name: ofTail_X
statement:
theorem ofTail_X (i : Fin n) :
    ofTail K n (Restricted.X K (1 : Fin n → ℝ) i) = Restricted.X K (1 : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.succ

name: ofTail_C
statement:
theorem ofTail_C (a : K) :
    ofTail K n (Restricted.C (1 : Fin n → ℝ) a) = Restricted.C (1 : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) a

name: norm_ofPolynomial_le_iff
statement:
theorem norm_ofPolynomial_le_iff {ε : ℝ} (p : Polynomial (TateAlgebra K n)) :
    ‖ofPolynomial K n p‖ ≤ ε ↔ ∀ i, ‖p.coeff i‖ ≤ ε
doc: /-- The Gauss norm of a polynomial in `X 0` is the maximum of the norms of its coefficients. -/

name: norm_ofTail
statement: theorem norm_ofTail (f : TateAlgebra K n) : ‖ofTail K n f‖ = ‖f‖

name: ne_zero_of_isMulDistinguishedX0
statement:
theorem ne_zero_of_isMulDistinguishedX0 {g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)} {s : ℕ}
    (hg : IsMulDistinguishedX0 g s) : g ≠ 0
doc: /-- A distinguished series is nonzero. -/

name: isMulDistinguishedX0_smul_iff
statement:
theorem isMulDistinguishedX0_smul_iff {a : K} (ha : a ≠ 0) {g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)} {s : ℕ} :
    IsMulDistinguishedX0 (a • g) s ↔ IsMulDistinguishedX0 g s
doc: /-- Distinguishedness is invariant under multiplication by a nonzero scalar. -/

name: isMulDistinguishedX0_zero_iff
statement:
theorem isMulDistinguishedX0_zero_iff [CompleteSpace K] {g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)} :
    IsMulDistinguishedX0 g 0 ↔ IsUnit g
doc:
/-- A series is `X 0`-distinguished of order `0` if and only if it is a unit.
Source: Bosch 1.2/6 ("an arbitrary series `g ∈ Tₙ` is `ζₙ`-distinguished of order `0` if and only
if it is a unit"). -/

name: coeff_finSuccEquiv_reduction
statement:
theorem coeff_finSuccEquiv_reduction (g : unitClosedBall (TateAlgebra K (n + 1))) (ν : ℕ) :
    (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv _ n (reduction g)).coeff ν =
      reduction ⟨coeffX0 (g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) ν,
        mem_unitClosedBall.2 ((norm_coeffX0_le _ ν).trans (Subring.norm_le_one g))⟩
doc:
/-- The coefficients in `X 0` of the reduction are the reductions of the coefficients in `X 0`.
Source: BGR 5.2.1 (reading `g̃` in `k̃[X₁, …, X_{n−1}][Xₙ]`). -/

name: isMulDistinguishedX0_iff_reduction
statement:
theorem isMulDistinguishedX0_iff_reduction [CompleteSpace K]
    {g : unitClosedBall (TateAlgebra K (n + 1))} (hg : ‖(g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1))‖ = 1)
    {s : ℕ} :
    IsMulDistinguishedX0 (g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) s ↔
      (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv _ n (reduction g)).natDegree = s ∧
        IsUnit (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv _ n (reduction g)).leadingCoeff
doc:
/-- A series of Gauss norm one is `X 0`-distinguished of order `s` if and only if its reduction,
as a polynomial in `X 0`, has degree `s` and a unit as leading coefficient. Source: BGR 5.2.1
("`g` with `|g| = 1` is `Xₙ`-distinguished of degree `s` if and only if `g̃` is a unitary polynomial
of degree `s`"); Bosch 1.2/6. -/

name: isWeierstrassPolynomial_iff
statement:
theorem isWeierstrassPolynomial_iff {ω : Polynomial (TateAlgebra K n)} :
    IsWeierstrassPolynomial K n ω ↔ ω.Monic ∧ ∀ i, ‖ω.coeff i‖ ≤ 1
doc:
/-- A monic polynomial is a Weierstrass polynomial if and only if its coefficients lie in the
unit ball. -/

name: isWeierstrassPolynomial_X_pow
statement:
theorem isWeierstrassPolynomial_X_pow (s : ℕ) :
    IsWeierstrassPolynomial K n (Polynomial.X ^ s)
doc: /-- The powers of the variable `X 0` are Weierstrass polynomials. -/

name: IsWeierstrassPolynomial.of_mul_left
doc:
/-- If a product of two monic polynomials is a Weierstrass polynomial, so is the left factor.
Source: BGR 5.2.3/2. -/

name: IsWeierstrassPolynomial.of_mul_right
doc:
/-- If a product of two monic polynomials is a Weierstrass polynomial, so is the right factor.
Source: BGR 5.2.3/2. -/

name: IsWeierstrassPolynomial.isMulDistinguishedX0
doc:
/-- A Weierstrass polynomial of degree `s` is `X 0`-distinguished of order `s`.
Source: BGR 5.2.2/1 ("`|ω| = 1` so that `ω` is `Xₙ`-distinguished of degree `s`"). -/

name: exists_isWeierstrassPolynomial_of_isMulDistinguishedX0
statement:
theorem exists_isWeierstrassPolynomial_of_isMulDistinguishedX0 [CompleteSpace K]
    {g : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)} {s : ℕ} (hg : IsMulDistinguishedX0 g s) :
    ∃ (ω : Polynomial (TateAlgebra K n)) (e : (TateAlgebra K (n + 1))ˣ),
      IsWeierstrassPolynomial K n ω ∧ ω.natDegree = s ∧ g = e * ofPolynomial K n ω

name: IsWeierstrassPolynomial.eq_of_mul_eq_mul
doc: /-- The Weierstrass polynomial of a distinguished series is unique. Source: BGR 5.2.2/1. -/

name: IsWeierstrassPolynomial.existsUnique_remainder
statement:
theorem IsWeierstrassPolynomial.existsUnique_remainder (hω : IsWeierstrassPolynomial K n ω)
    (f : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) :
    ∃! r : Polynomial (TateAlgebra K n),
      r.degree < ω.degree ∧ f - ofPolynomial K n r ∈ Ideal.span {ofPolynomial K n ω}
doc:
/-- Modulo a Weierstrass polynomial `ω` every series has a unique representative that is a
polynomial in `X 0` of degree less than `deg ω`: the quotient `T_{n+1} ⧸ (ω)` is free over `Tₙ` on
`1, X 0, …, X 0 ^ (deg ω - 1)`. Source: BGR 5.2.3/3 (i). -/

name: IsWeierstrassPolynomial.bijective_quotientMap
statement:
theorem IsWeierstrassPolynomial.bijective_quotientMap (hω : IsWeierstrassPolynomial K n ω) :
    Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap ((Ideal.span {ω}).map (ofPolynomial K n)) (ofPolynomial K n)
        Ideal.le_comap_map)
doc:
/-- The quotient of the Tate algebra by a Weierstrass polynomial is the quotient of the polynomial
ring: the natural map `Tₙ[X] ⧸ (ω) → T_{n+1} ⧸ (ω)` is bijective. Source: BGR 5.2.3/3 (ii). -/

name: IsWeierstrassPolynomial.finite_mk_comp_ofTail
statement:
theorem IsWeierstrassPolynomial.finite_mk_comp_ofTail (hω : IsWeierstrassPolynomial K n ω) :
    ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {ofPolynomial K n ω})).comp (ofTail K n)).Finite
doc:
/-- The map `Tₙ → T_{n+1} ⧸ (ω)` is finite for every Weierstrass polynomial `ω`.
Source: BGR 5.2.3/4 ("In particular, …"). -/

name: IsWeierstrassPolynomial.injective_mk_comp_ofTail
statement:
theorem IsWeierstrassPolynomial.injective_mk_comp_ofTail (hω : IsWeierstrassPolynomial K n ω)
    (hdeg : 0 < ω.natDegree) :
    Function.Injective
      ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {ofPolynomial K n ω})).comp (ofTail K n))
doc:
/-- The map `Tₙ → T_{n+1} ⧸ (ω)` is injective for every Weierstrass polynomial `ω` of positive
degree. -/

name: IsWeierstrassPolynomial.finite_comp_ofTail
statement:
theorem IsWeierstrassPolynomial.finite_comp_ofTail (hω : IsWeierstrassPolynomial K n ω)
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (φ : TateAlgebra K (n + 1) →+* A) (hφ : φ.Finite)
    (h0 : φ (ofPolynomial K n ω) = 0) : (φ.comp (ofTail K n)).Finite
doc:
/-- **Weierstrass finiteness theorem**: a finite ring homomorphism out of `T_{n+1}` whose kernel
contains a Weierstrass polynomial restricts to a finite homomorphism on `Tₙ`.
Source: BGR 5.2.3/4. -/

name: finite_mk_comp_ofTail_of_isMulDistinguishedX0
doc:
/-- The map `Tₙ → T_{n+1} ⧸ (g)` is finite for every `X 0`-distinguished series `g`.
Source: BGR 5.2.3/4; Bosch 1.2/10 ("the canonical morphism `T_{n−1} → Tₙ → Tₙ/(g)` is finite"). -/

name: IsWeierstrassPolynomial.finite_compHom
statement:
theorem IsWeierstrassPolynomial.finite_compHom (hω : IsWeierstrassPolynomial K n ω)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) M]
    [Module.Finite (TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) M] (h : ∀ m : M, ofPolynomial K n ω • m = 0) :
    @Module.Finite (TateAlgebra K n) M _ _ (Module.compHom M (ofTail K n))
doc:
/-- Module form of the Weierstrass finiteness theorem: a finite `T_{n+1}`-module killed by a
Weierstrass polynomial is finite over `Tₙ`. Source: BGR 5.2.3/4. -/

name: shearAlgHom_comp_shearAlgHom
statement:
theorem shearAlgHom_comp_shearAlgHom (e : Fin n → ℕ) {a b : R} (hab : a + b = 0) :
    (shearAlgHom R e a).comp (shearAlgHom R e b) = AlgHom.id R _

name: shear_X_zero
statement: theorem shear_X_zero (e : Fin n → ℕ) : shear R e (X 0) = X 0

name: shear_X_succ
statement:
theorem shear_X_succ (e : Fin n → ℕ) (i : Fin n) :
    shear R e (X i.succ) = X i.succ + X 0 ^ e i

name: sum_pow_mul_ne_of_lt
statement:
theorem sum_pow_mul_ne_of_lt {t : ℕ} {v w : Fin (n + 1) →₀ ℕ} (hv : ∀ i, v i < t)
    (hw : ∀ i, w i < t) (hvw : v ≠ w) :
    ∑ i : Fin (n + 1), t ^ i.val * v i ≠ ∑ i : Fin (n + 1), t ^ i.val * w i
doc:
/-- Distinct exponent vectors with entries below `t` have distinct weighted degrees
`Σ t ^ i * v i`: the base-`t` expansion is unique. -/

name: degreeOf_zero_shear_monomial
doc: /-- The degree in `X 0` of the shear of a monomial. -/

name: leadingCoeff_finSuccEquiv_shear_monomial
statement:
theorem leadingCoeff_finSuccEquiv_shear_monomial {e : Fin n → ℕ} (he : ∀ i, 0 < e i)
    (v : Fin (n + 1) →₀ ℕ) (a : k) :
    (finSuccEquiv k n ((shear k e) (monomial v a))).leadingCoeff = C a
doc:
/-- For positive exponents, the leading coefficient in `X 0` of the shear of a monomial is its
coefficient. -/

name: isUnit_leadingCoeff_finSuccEquiv_shear
statement:
theorem isUnit_leadingCoeff_finSuccEquiv_shear {f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) k} (hf : f ≠ 0)
    {t : ℕ} (ht : ∀ v ∈ f.support, ∀ i, v i < t) :
    IsUnit (finSuccEquiv k n (shear k (fun i : Fin n ↦ t ^ (i.val + 1)) f)).leadingCoeff
doc:
/-- After the shear with exponents `t ^ (i + 1)`, for `t` exceeding every exponent of a nonzero
polynomial `f` over a field, the leading coefficient of `f` in `X 0` is a unit.
Source: BGR 5.2.4/1 (the computation of `σ̃(f̃)`); Bosch 1.2/7. -/

name: norm_shearTuple_le_one
statement:
theorem norm_shearTuple_le_one (e : Fin n → ℕ) {a : K} (ha : ‖a‖ ≤ 1) (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
    ‖shearTuple K n e a i‖ ≤ 1

name: shearAlgHom_comp_shearAlgHom
statement:
theorem shearAlgHom_comp_shearAlgHom (e : Fin n → ℕ) {a b : K} (ha : ‖a‖ ≤ 1) (hb : ‖b‖ ≤ 1)
    (hab : a + b = 0) :
    (shearAlgHom K n e a ha).comp (shearAlgHom K n e b hb) = AlgHom.id K _

name: shear_X_zero
statement:
theorem shear_X_zero (e : Fin n → ℕ) :
    shear K n e (Restricted.X K (1 : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) 0) =
      Restricted.X K (1 : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) 0

name: shear_X_succ
statement:
theorem shear_X_succ (e : Fin n → ℕ) (i : Fin n) :
    shear K n e (Restricted.X K (1 : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.succ) =
      Restricted.X K (1 : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.succ +
        Restricted.X K (1 : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) 0 ^ e i

name: norm_shear
statement: theorem norm_shear (e : Fin n → ℕ) (f : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)) : ‖shear K n e f‖ = ‖f‖
doc:
/-- The shear is an isometry for the Gauss norm. Source: BGR 5.1.3 (Example: "`φ` is an isometric
automorphism of `Tₙ`"); Bosch 1.2/7 ("`|σ(f)| = |f|` for all `f ∈ Tₙ`"). -/

name: reduction_shear
statement:
theorem reduction_shear (e : Fin n → ℕ) (f : unitClosedBall (TateAlgebra K (n + 1))) :
    reduction ⟨shear K n e (f : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)),
        mem_unitClosedBall.2 ((norm_shear e _).trans_le (Subring.norm_le_one f))⟩ =
      MvPolynomial.shear _ e (reduction f)
doc:
/-- The reduction of the shear is the shear of the reduction. Source: BGR 5.2.4/1
("`(σ(f))~ = σ̃(f̃)`"). -/

name: exists_isMulDistinguishedX0_shear
doc:
/-- **Distinguished charts, explicit form**: for `t` exceeding every exponent occurring at a
coefficient of `f` of maximal norm, the shear with exponents `t ^ (i + 1)` makes `f`
`X 0`-distinguished. Source: BGR 5.2.4/2; Bosch 1.2/7. -/

name: exists_shear_isMulDistinguishedX0
statement:
theorem exists_shear_isMulDistinguishedX0 {f : TateAlgebra K (n + 1)} (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (e : Fin n → ℕ) (s : ℕ), IsMulDistinguishedX0 (shear K n e f) s
doc:
/-- **Distinguished charts**: every nonzero series becomes `X 0`-distinguished after a shear.
Source: BGR 5.2.4/1. -/

name: exists_shear_forall_isMulDistinguishedX0
statement:
theorem exists_shear_forall_isMulDistinguishedX0 (F : Finset (TateAlgebra K (n + 1)))
    (hF : ∀ f ∈ F, f ≠ 0) :
    ∃ e : Fin n → ℕ, ∀ f ∈ F, ∃ s, IsMulDistinguishedX0 (shear K n e f) s
doc:
/-- Finitely many nonzero series become `X 0`-distinguished after one and the same shear.
Source: Bosch 1.2/7. -/

name: ringKrullDim_le_of_isIntegral
statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_le_of_isIntegral {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S)
    (hf : f.IsIntegral) : ringKrullDim S ≤ ringKrullDim R
doc:
/-- An integral ring homomorphism does not raise the Krull dimension: distinct comparable primes
have distinct contractions. Source: BGR 6.1.2 (Remark), citing Nagata, Corollary 10.10. -/

name: ringKrullDim_le_add_one_of_forall_quotient_le
statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_le_add_one_of_forall_quotient_le {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {d : WithBot ℕ∞}
    (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (h : ∀ p q : Ideal R, p.IsPrime → q.IsPrime → q < p → ringKrullDim (R ⧸ p) ≤ d) :
    ringKrullDim R ≤ d + 1
doc:
/-- If the quotient by every prime that is not minimal has Krull dimension at most `d`, the ring
has Krull dimension at most `d + 1`. -/

name: finite_mk_comp_C
statement:
theorem finite_mk_comp_C (h : IsRueckert φ W) {ω : I[X]} (hω : ω ∈ W) :
    ((Ideal.Quotient.mk ((Ideal.span {ω}).map φ)).comp (φ.comp C)).Finite
doc:
/-- For `ω ∈ W` the canonical map `I → I' ⧸ (ω)` is finite. Source: BGR 5.2.5/1 ("In particular,
the canonical map `I → I'/ωI'` is finite"). -/

name: exists_ringEquiv_mem_map
statement:
theorem exists_ringEquiv_mem_map (h : IsRueckert φ W) {a : Ideal I'} (ha : a ≠ ⊥) :
    ∃ (σ : I' ≃+* I') (ω : I[X]), ω ∈ W ∧ φ ω ∈ a.map (σ : I' →+* I')
doc:
/-- Every nonzero ideal of a Rückert overring contains, after an automorphism, a member of `W`.
Source: BGR 5.2.5/2 ("According to axiom (3), we may assume that `𝔞` contains a polynomial
`ω ∈ W`"). -/

name: isNoetherianRing
statement: theorem isNoetherianRing (h : IsRueckert φ W) [IsNoetherianRing I] : IsNoetherianRing I'
doc: /-- A Rückert overring of a noetherian ring is noetherian. Source: BGR 5.2.5/2. -/

name: jacobson_eq_radical
statement:
theorem jacobson_eq_radical (h : IsRueckert φ W) [IsJacobsonRing I] {a : Ideal I'} (ha : a ≠ ⊥) :
    a.jacobson = a.radical
doc:
/-- In a Rückert overring of a Jacobson ring, the nilradical of a nonzero ideal is its Jacobson
radical. Source: BGR 5.2.5/3. -/

name: isJacobsonRing
statement:
theorem isJacobsonRing (h : IsRueckert φ W) [IsJacobsonRing I]
    (h0 : (⊥ : Ideal I').jacobson = ⊥) : IsJacobsonRing I'
doc:
/-- A Rückert overring of a Jacobson ring whose Jacobson radical vanishes is a Jacobson ring.
Source: BGR 5.2.6/3. -/

name: uniqueFactorizationMonoid
statement:
theorem uniqueFactorizationMonoid (h : IsRueckert φ W) [IsDomain I]
    [UniqueFactorizationMonoid I] [IsDomain I'] : UniqueFactorizationMonoid I'
doc:
/-- An integral domain which is Rückert over a factorial ring is factorial.
Source: BGR 5.2.5/4. -/

name: ringKrullDim_quotient_le
statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_quotient_le (h : IsRueckert φ W) {ω : I[X]} (hω : ω ∈ W) :
    ringKrullDim (I' ⧸ (Ideal.span {ω}).map φ) ≤ ringKrullDim I
doc:
/-- For `ω ∈ W` the Krull dimension of `I' ⧸ (ω)` is at most that of `I`. Source: Bosch 1.2/10
("the canonical morphism `T_{n−1} → Tₙ → Tₙ/(g)` is finite"). -/

name: ringKrullDim_le
statement: theorem ringKrullDim_le (h : IsRueckert φ W) : ringKrullDim I' ≤ ringKrullDim I + 1
doc:
/-- The Krull dimension of a Rückert overring is at most that of the base plus one.
Source: Bosch 1.2/10 (the descent `T_{n−1} → Tₙ/(g)` finite), BGR 6.1.2 (Remark). -/

name: ringKrullDim_add_one_le
statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_add_one_le (h : IsRueckert φ W) [IsDomain I'] (hX : (X : I[X]) ∈ W) :
    ringKrullDim I + 1 ≤ ringKrullDim I'
doc:
/-- If the variable `X` belongs to `W` and `I'` is a domain, the Krull dimension of a Rückert
overring is at least that of the base plus one. Source: BGR 6.1.2 (Remark: the chain
`0 ⊂ (X₁) ⊂ (X₁, X₂) ⊂ …`). -/

name: isRueckert_ofPolynomial
doc:
/-- The Tate algebra in `n + 1` variables is Rückert over the Tate algebra in `n` variables, for
the family of Weierstrass polynomials in `X 0`. Source: BGR 5.2.5 ("According to the results of
(5.2.2), (5.2.3) and (5.2.4), the algebra `Tₙ` is Rückert over `T_{n−1}`"), 5.2.6. -/

name: instIsNoetherianRing
statement:
instance instIsNoetherianRing (K : Type*) [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K]
    (n : ℕ) : IsNoetherianRing (TateAlgebra K n)
doc: /-- **The Tate algebra is noetherian.** Source: BGR 5.2.6/1; Bosch 1.2/13. -/

name: instUniqueFactorizationMonoid
statement:
instance instUniqueFactorizationMonoid (K : Type*) [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K]
    [CompleteSpace K] (n : ℕ) : UniqueFactorizationMonoid (TateAlgebra K n)
doc: /-- **The Tate algebra is factorial.** Source: BGR 5.2.6/1; Bosch 1.2/14. -/

name: instIsJacobsonRing
statement:
instance instIsJacobsonRing (K : Type*) [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K]
    (n : ℕ) : IsJacobsonRing (TateAlgebra K n)
doc: /-- **The Tate algebra is a Jacobson ring.** Source: BGR 5.2.6/3; Bosch 1.2/15. -/

name: ringKrullDim_eq
statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_eq (K : Type*) [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K]
    (n : ℕ) : ringKrullDim (TateAlgebra K n) = n
doc:
/-- **The Krull dimension of the Tate algebra `Tₙ` is `n`.** Source: BGR 6.1.2 (Remark);
Bosch 1.2/10. -/

name: IsBald.mono
statement: theorem IsBald.mono {S S' : Subring K} (h : S ≤ S') (hS' : S'.IsBald) : S.IsBald
doc: /-- A subring of a bald subring is bald. -/

name: le_unitLocalization
statement: theorem le_unitLocalization (S : Subring K) : S ≤ S.unitLocalization

name: mem_unitLocalization_iff
statement:
theorem mem_unitLocalization_iff {S : Subring K} {x : K} :
    x ∈ S.unitLocalization ↔ ∃ s ∈ S, ∃ u ∈ S, ‖u‖ = 1 ∧ x = s / u
doc: /-- The elements of the localisation are the fractions with denominator of norm one. -/

name: IsBald.unitLocalization
statement: theorem IsBald.unitLocalization {S : Subring K} (hS : S.IsBald) : S.unitLocalization.IsBald
doc: /-- The localisation of a bald subring at its elements of norm one is bald. -/

name: isBRing_unitLocalization
statement:
theorem isBRing_unitLocalization {S : Subring K} (hS : ∀ a ∈ S, ‖a‖ ≤ 1) :
    S.unitLocalization.IsBRing
doc: /-- The localisation at the elements of norm one is a B-ring. -/

name: isBald_bot
statement: theorem isBald_bot : (⊥ : Subring K).IsBald
doc:
/-- The prime subring of a nonarchimedean field is bald. Source: Bosch 1.3/3 ("The smallest subring
`S ⊂ R` equals either `ℤ/pℤ` for some prime `p`, or `ℤ`. It is bald"). -/

name: IsBald.closure_union_of_norm_le
statement:
theorem IsBald.closure_union_of_norm_le {S : Subring K} (hS : S.IsBald) {T : Set K} {ε : ℝ}
    (hε : ε < 1) (hT : ∀ x ∈ T, ‖x‖ ≤ ε) : (closure ((S : Set K) ∪ T)).IsBald
doc:
/-- Adjoining elements of norm at most `ε < 1` to a bald subring gives a bald subring.
Source: Bosch 1.3/3 ("If there is an `ε ∈ R` such that `|aₙ| ≤ ε < 1` for all `n`, we see for
trivial reasons that `S[a₀, a₁, …]` is bald"). -/

name: IsBRing.exists_monic_norm_aeval_lt_one
statement:
theorem IsBRing.exists_monic_norm_aeval_lt_one {S : Subring K} (hS : S.IsBRing) {a : K}
    (ha : ‖a‖ = 1) {p : Polynomial S} (hp : ‖Polynomial.aeval a p‖ < 1)
    (hc : ∃ i, ‖(p.coeff i : K)‖ = 1) :
    ∃ g : Polynomial S, g.Monic ∧ g.natDegree ≤ p.natDegree ∧ ‖Polynomial.aeval a g‖ < 1
doc:
/-- In a B-ring `S`, a polynomial with a coefficient of norm one whose value at an element `a` of
norm one is small gives a monic polynomial of no larger degree with the same property. -/

name: IsBRing.isBald_closure_insert
statement:
theorem IsBRing.isBald_closure_insert {S : Subring K} (hB : S.IsBRing) (hS : S.IsBald) {a : K}
    (ha : ‖a‖ = 1) : (closure (insert a (S : Set K))).IsBald
doc:
/-- Adjoining an element of norm one to a bald B-ring gives a bald subring. Source: Bosch 1.3/3
(the transcendental and the algebraic case). -/

name: IsBald.closure_insert
statement:
theorem IsBald.closure_insert {S : Subring K} (hS : S.IsBald) {a : K} (ha : ‖a‖ ≤ 1) :
    (closure (insert a (S : Set K))).IsBald
doc:
/-- Adjoining an element of the unit ball to a bald subring gives a bald subring.
Source: Bosch 1.3/3 ("it is enough to show that, for a bald subring `S ⊂ R` and an element
`a ∈ R` of value `|a| = 1`, the ring `S[a]` is bald"). -/

name: isBald_closure_range
statement:
theorem isBald_closure_range {ι : Type*} {a : ι → K} (ha : ∀ i, ‖a i‖ ≤ 1)
    (ha0 : Tendsto a cofinite (𝓝 0)) : (closure (Set.range a)).IsBald
doc: /-- **The subring generated by a null family of the unit ball is bald.** Source: Bosch 1.3/3. -/

name: norm_coeff_le_norm_sum
statement:
theorem norm_coeff_le_norm_sum (he : IsOrthonormalFamily K e) (s : Finset I) (a : I → K) {i : I}
    (hi : i ∈ s) : ‖a i‖ ≤ ‖∑ j ∈ s, a j • e j‖
doc:
/-- In a finite combination of an orthonormal family every coefficient is bounded by the norm of
the combination. -/

name: norm_sum_le
statement:
theorem norm_sum_le (he : IsOrthonormalFamily K e) (s : Finset I) (a : I → K) {C : ℝ}
    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (h : ∀ i ∈ s, ‖a i‖ ≤ C) : ‖∑ i ∈ s, a i • e i‖ ≤ C
doc: /-- A finite combination of an orthonormal family is bounded by any bound on its coefficients. -/

name: linearIndependent
statement: theorem linearIndependent (he : IsOrthonormalFamily K e) : LinearIndependent K e
doc: /-- An orthonormal family is linearly independent. -/

name: tendsto_cofinite_of_hasSum
statement:
theorem tendsto_cofinite_of_hasSum (he : IsOrthonormalFamily K e) {a : I → K} {x : V}
    (hx : HasSum (fun i ↦ a i • e i) x) : Tendsto a cofinite (𝓝 0)
doc: /-- The coefficients of a convergent expansion in an orthonormal family tend to zero. -/

name: norm_coeff_le_of_hasSum
statement:
theorem norm_coeff_le_of_hasSum (he : IsOrthonormalFamily K e) {a : I → K} {x : V}
    (hx : HasSum (fun i ↦ a i • e i) x) (i : I) : ‖a i‖ ≤ ‖x‖
doc:
/-- In a convergent expansion in an orthonormal family every coefficient is bounded by the norm of
the sum. Source: Bosch 1.3/5 (iii). -/

name: norm_le_of_hasSum
statement:
theorem norm_le_of_hasSum (he : IsOrthonormalFamily K e) {a : I → K} {x : V}
    (hx : HasSum (fun i ↦ a i • e i) x) {C : ℝ} (hC : 0 ≤ C) (h : ∀ i, ‖a i‖ ≤ C) : ‖x‖ ≤ C
doc:
/-- A convergent expansion in an orthonormal family is bounded by any bound on its coefficients.
Source: Bosch 1.3/5 (iii). -/

name: eq_of_hasSum
statement:
theorem eq_of_hasSum (he : IsOrthonormalFamily K e) {a b : I → K} {x : V}
    (ha : HasSum (fun i ↦ a i • e i) x) (hb : HasSum (fun i ↦ b i • e i) x) : a = b
doc:
/-- The coefficients of an expansion in an orthonormal family are unique.
Source: Bosch 1.3/5 ("In particular, the coefficients `c_ν` in (ii) are unique"). -/

name: summable_smul
statement:
theorem summable_smul [IsUltrametricDist V] [CompleteSpace V] (he : IsOrthonormalFamily K e)
    {a : I → K} (ha : Tendsto a cofinite (𝓝 0)) : Summable fun i ↦ a i • e i
doc:
/-- In a complete nonarchimedean space a family of coefficients tending to zero is summable against
an orthonormal family. -/

name: exists_hasSum
statement:
theorem exists_hasSum [CompleteSpace K] (he : IsOrthonormalBasis K e) (x : V) :
    ∃ a : I → K, HasSum (fun i ↦ a i • e i) x
doc:
/-- Every vector of a complete nonarchimedean space over a complete field has an expansion in an
orthonormal basis. Source: Bosch 1.3/5 (ii).

Completeness of the field is necessary: `ℚ_[p]` is a complete normed space over `ℚ` with its
`p`-adic norm, the family `{1}` is orthonormal with dense span, and an element of `ℚ_[p]` outside
`ℚ` has no expansion. -/

name: Finsupp.mem_span_range_of_mapRange_mem_span
statement:
theorem Finsupp.mem_span_range_of_mapRange_mem_span {F E : Type*} [Field F] [Field E]
    [Algebra F E] {N M : Type*} (v : M → N →₀ F) (w : N →₀ F)
    (h : Finsupp.mapRange (algebraMap F E) (map_zero _) w ∈
      Submodule.span E (Set.range fun μ ↦ Finsupp.mapRange (algebraMap F E) (map_zero _) (v μ))) :
    w ∈ Submodule.span F (Set.range v)
doc:
/-- A vector with coefficients in a subfield `F` that lies in the span over the field `E` of a
family of vectors with coefficients in `F` lies in its span over `F`. -/

name: Subring.IsBRing.residueSubfield
statement:
def Subring.IsBRing.residueSubfield {S : Subring K} (hS : S.IsBRing) :
    Subfield (ResidueField (unitClosedBall K)) where
doc:
/-- The image of a B-ring in the residue field of `K` is a subfield. Source: Bosch 1.3/3 ("Then
`S` contains a unique maximal ideal `𝔪`, and `S̃ = S/𝔪` is a field"). -/

name: IsOrthonormalFamily.of_linearIndependent_residue
statement:
theorem IsOrthonormalFamily.of_linearIndependent_residue (hx : IsOrthonormalFamily K x)
    (hy : ∀ μ, HasSum (fun ν ↦ c μ ν • x ν) (y μ)) (hc : ∀ μ ν, ‖c μ ν‖ ≤ 1)
    (r : M → N →₀ ResidueField (unitClosedBall K))
    (hr : ∀ μ ν, r μ ν = residue (unitClosedBall K) ⟨c μ ν, mem_unitClosedBall.2 (hc μ ν)⟩)
    (hli : LinearIndependent (ResidueField (unitClosedBall K)) r) : IsOrthonormalFamily K y
doc:
/-- A family of the unit ball whose reductions are linearly independent over the residue field is
orthonormal. Source: Bosch 1.3/6 ("In particular, `(y_μ)` is an orthonormal basis of a subspace
`V' ⊂ V`"). -/

name: exists_norm_sub_le_of_span_residue
statement:
theorem exists_norm_sub_le_of_span_residue (hx : IsOrthonormalFamily K x)
    (hy : ∀ μ, HasSum (fun ν ↦ c μ ν • x ν) (y μ)) {S : Subring K} (hS : S.IsBald)
    (hcS : ∀ μ ν, c μ ν ∈ S) (r : M → N →₀ ResidueField (unitClosedBall K))
    (hr : ∀ μ ν, r μ ν = residue (unitClosedBall K)
      ⟨c μ ν, mem_unitClosedBall.2 (hS.norm_le_one _ (hcS μ ν))⟩)
    (hspan : Submodule.span (ResidueField (unitClosedBall K)) (Set.range r) = ⊤) :
    ∃ ε : ℝ, ε < 1 ∧ ∀ ν, ∃ z ∈ Submodule.span K (Set.range y), ‖x ν - z‖ ≤ ε
doc:
/-- If the reductions of the `y μ` span the reduction of `V` and the coordinates of the `y μ` lie
in a bald subring, then every basis vector `x ν` is approximated by the span of `y` up to a uniform
`ε < 1`. Source: Bosch 1.3/6 ("for any `x_ν`, there is an element `z_ν ∈ V'_S` satisfying
`|x_ν − z_ν| ≤ ε`"). -/

name: dense_span_of_forall_exists_norm_sub_le
doc:
/-- If every vector of an orthonormal basis is approximated by a subspace up to a uniform `ε < 1`,
the subspace is dense. Source: Bosch 1.3/6 ("for any `x ∈ V_S`, there is an element `z ∈ V'_S`
with `|x − z| ≤ ε|x|`. But then … we get `V'_S = V_S` by iteration"); BGR 1.1.4/2. -/

name: IsOrthonormalBasis.of_residue_basis
statement:
theorem IsOrthonormalBasis.of_residue_basis (hx : IsOrthonormalBasis K x)
    (hy : ∀ μ, HasSum (fun ν ↦ c μ ν • x ν) (y μ)) {S : Subring K} (hS : S.IsBald)
    (hcS : ∀ μ ν, c μ ν ∈ S) (r : M → N →₀ ResidueField (unitClosedBall K))
    (hr : ∀ μ ν, r μ ν = residue (unitClosedBall K)
      ⟨c μ ν, mem_unitClosedBall.2 (hS.norm_le_one _ (hcS μ ν))⟩)
    (hli : LinearIndependent (ResidueField (unitClosedBall K)) r)
    (hspan : Submodule.span (ResidueField (unitClosedBall K)) (Set.range r) = ⊤) :
    IsOrthonormalBasis K y
doc:
/-- **Lifting of orthonormal bases.** Let `x` be an orthonormal basis of a nonarchimedean space
`V` and `y` a family whose coordinates `c μ ν` with respect to `x` lie in a bald subring. If
the reductions of the `y μ` form a basis of the reduction of `V` over the residue field, then `y`
is an orthonormal basis of `V`. Source: Bosch 1.3/6. -/

name: exists_basis_adaptedFamily
statement:
theorem exists_basis_adaptedFamily [Fintype ι] {r : ℕ} (h : Fin r → ι → MvPolynomial σ k) :
    ∃ (A : Set ((σ →₀ ℕ) × Fin r)) (B : Set (Σ _ : ι, σ →₀ ℕ)),
      LinearIndependent k (adaptedFamily h A B) ∧
        Submodule.span k (Set.range (adaptedFamily h A B)) = ⊤ ∧
          Submodule.span k (Set.range fun a : A ↦ monomial a.1.1 (1 : k) • h a.1.2) =
            (Submodule.span (MvPolynomial σ k) (Set.range h)).restrictScalars k
doc:
/-- For finitely many vectors `h j` of a free module `k[X]^ι` there are monomial multiples
`X^ν • h j` forming a `k`-basis of the submodule they generate, and monomial vectors completing
them to a `k`-basis of `k[X]^ι`. Source: Bosch 1.3/7 and 1.3/10 ("we can find a system `(y_μ)` of
elements of type `ζ^ν aᵢ` such that its residue classes form a `k`-basis of `ã`. Adding monomials
of type `ζ^ν` …"). -/

name: isOrthonormalBasis_monomial
statement:
theorem isOrthonormalBasis_monomial :
    IsOrthonormalBasis K fun t : σ →₀ ℕ ↦ (monomial (1 : σ → ℝ) t (1 : K) : 𝕋)
doc:
/-- The monomials are an orthonormal basis of the Tate algebra as a normed `K`-vector space.
Source: Bosch 1.3/5 ("the monomials `ζ^ν ∈ Tₙ` form an orthonormal basis"); BGR 5.1.1/4. -/

name: isOrthonormalBasis_single_monomial
statement:
theorem isOrthonormalBasis_single_monomial :
    IsOrthonormalBasis K fun p : (Σ _ : ι, σ →₀ ℕ) ↦
      (Pi.single p.1 (monomial (1 : σ → ℝ) p.2 (1 : K)) : ι → 𝕋)
doc:
/-- The monomial vectors `X^ν eᵢ` are an orthonormal basis of the free module `Tˢ` with the
maximum norm. Source: Bosch 1.3/10 ("the canonical system `Z = (ζ^ν eⱼ)`, which is an orthonormal
basis of `Tₙˢ`"). -/

name: hasSum_coeff_smul_single_monomial
statement:
theorem hasSum_coeff_smul_single_monomial (f : ι → 𝕋) :
    HasSum (fun p : (Σ _ : ι, σ →₀ ℕ) ↦
      coeff p.2 (f p.1).1 • (Pi.single p.1 (monomial (1 : σ → ℝ) p.2 (1 : K)) : ι → 𝕋)) f
doc: /-- The expansion of a tuple of series in the monomial vectors. -/

name: reductionPi_eq_zero_iff
statement: theorem reductionPi_eq_zero_iff {x : ι → 𝕋} (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ 1) : reductionPi x hx = 0 ↔ ‖x‖ < 1
doc: /-- The reduction vanishes exactly on the tuples of norm less than one. -/

name: reductionSubmodule
statement:
def reductionSubmodule (N : Submodule 𝕋 (ι → 𝕋)) :
    Submodule (MvPolynomial σ 𝕜) (ι → MvPolynomial σ 𝕜) where
doc:
/-- The reduction `Ñ` of a submodule `N` of `Tˢ`: the reductions of the elements of `N` in the
unit ball, a submodule of `k[X]ˢ`. Source: Bosch 1.3/10 ("Writing `Ñ` for the image of
`N ∩ (R⟨ζ⟩)ˢ`, we see that `Ñ` is a `k[ζ]`-submodule of `(k[ζ])ˢ`"). -/

name: exists_generators_reductionSubmodule
statement:
theorem exists_generators_reductionSubmodule [Finite σ] (N : Submodule 𝕋 (ι → 𝕋)) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (g : Fin r → ι → 𝕋) (hg : ∀ j, ‖g j‖ = 1), (∀ j, g j ∈ N) ∧
      Submodule.span (MvPolynomial σ 𝕜) (Set.range fun j ↦ reductionPi (g j) (hg j).le) =
        reductionSubmodule N
doc:
/-- The reduction of a submodule is generated by the reductions of finitely many of its elements
of norm one. Source: Bosch 1.3/10 ("we can choose elements `x₁, …, x_r ∈ N` of norm `1` such that
their residue classes generate `Ñ` as `k[ζ]`-module"). -/

name: exists_isBald_forall_coeff_mem
statement:
theorem exists_isBald_forall_coeff_mem {r : ℕ} (g : Fin r → ι → 𝕋) (hg : ∀ j, ‖g j‖ ≤ 1) :
    ∃ S : Subring K, S.IsBald ∧ ∀ j i t, coeff t (g j i).1 ∈ S
doc:
/-- The coefficients of finitely many tuples of the unit ball lie in a bald subring.
Source: Bosch 1.3/10 ("we need finitely many zero sequences in `R`, and the smallest subring
`R' ⊂ R` containing all these coefficients is bald by Proposition 3"). -/

name: isOrthonormalBasis_adaptedFamily
statement:
theorem isOrthonormalBasis_adaptedFamily {r : ℕ} {g : Fin r → ι → 𝕋} (hg : ∀ j, ‖g j‖ = 1)
    {A : Set ((σ →₀ ℕ) × Fin r)} {B : Set (Σ _ : ι, σ →₀ ℕ)}
    (hli : LinearIndependent 𝕜
      (MvPolynomial.adaptedFamily (fun j ↦ reductionPi (g j) (hg j).le) A B))
    (hspan : Submodule.span 𝕜
      (Set.range (MvPolynomial.adaptedFamily (fun j ↦ reductionPi (g j) (hg j).le) A B)) = ⊤) :
    IsOrthonormalBasis K (adaptedFamily g A B)
doc:
/-- If the reductions of an adapted family are a basis of `k[X]ˢ` over the residue field, the
adapted family is an orthonormal basis of `Tˢ`. Source: Bosch 1.3/10 ("Thus, by Theorem 6,
`(y_μ)` is an orthonormal basis of `Tₙˢ`"). -/

name: exists_eq_sum_smul_of_hasSum
statement:
theorem exists_eq_sum_smul_of_hasSum [CompleteSpace K] {r : ℕ} (g : Fin r → ι → 𝕋)
    {A : Set ((σ →₀ ℕ) × Fin r)} {c : A → K} {a : ι → 𝕋}
    (ha : HasSum (fun μ : A ↦ c μ • (monomial (1 : σ → ℝ) μ.1.1 (1 : K) • g μ.1.2)) a)
    (hc0 : Tendsto c cofinite (𝓝 0)) {C : ℝ} (hC0 : 0 ≤ C) (hC : ∀ μ, ‖c μ‖ ≤ C) :
    ∃ q : Fin r → 𝕋, (∀ j, ‖q j‖ ≤ C) ∧ a = ∑ j, q j • g j
doc:
/-- A convergent combination of multiples `X^ν • g j` with coefficients bounded by `C` is a
combination `Σ qⱼ • gⱼ` with `‖qⱼ‖ ≤ C`. Source: Bosch 1.3/7 ("we can write `f' = Σ fᵢaᵢ` with
certain elements `fᵢ ∈ Tₙ` satisfying `|fᵢ| ≤ |f|`"). -/

name: coeff_inr_eq_zero_of_mem
statement:
theorem coeff_inr_eq_zero_of_mem [CompleteSpace K] {N : Submodule 𝕋 (ι → 𝕋)} {r : ℕ}
    {g : Fin r → ι → 𝕋} (hg : ∀ j, ‖g j‖ = 1) (hgN : ∀ j, g j ∈ N)
    {A : Set ((σ →₀ ℕ) × Fin r)} {B : Set (Σ _ : ι, σ →₀ ℕ)}
    (hON : IsOrthonormalBasis K (adaptedFamily g A B))
    (hli : LinearIndependent 𝕜
      (MvPolynomial.adaptedFamily (fun j ↦ reductionPi (g j) (hg j).le) A B))
    (hA : Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range fun a : A ↦
        MvPolynomial.monomial a.1.1 (1 : 𝕜) • reductionPi (g a.1.2) (hg a.1.2).le) =
      (reductionSubmodule N).restrictScalars 𝕜)
    {x : ι → 𝕋} (hx : x ∈ N) {c : A ⊕ B → K}
    (hc : HasSum (fun μ ↦ c μ • adaptedFamily g A B μ) x) (b : B) : c (Sum.inr b) = 0
doc:
/-- For an adapted orthonormal basis whose part in `N` reduces to a basis of the reduction of `N`,
the expansion of an element of `N` involves only the part in `N`. Source: Bosch 1.3/7 ("we may
replace `f` by `f − f'` … and thereby assume `c_μ = 0` for `μ ∈ M'`. Then, if `f ≠ 0` … we would
get a non-trivial equation … which, however, contradicts the construction"). -/

name: exists_isOrthonormalBasis_adaptedFamily
statement:
theorem exists_isOrthonormalBasis_adaptedFamily [Finite σ] [CompleteSpace K]
    (N : Submodule 𝕋 (ι → 𝕋)) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (g : Fin r → ι → 𝕋) (A : Set ((σ →₀ ℕ) × Fin r)) (B : Set (Σ _ : ι, σ →₀ ℕ)),
      (∀ j, g j ∈ N) ∧ (∀ j, ‖g j‖ = 1) ∧ IsOrthonormalBasis K (adaptedFamily g A B) ∧
        ∀ x ∈ N, ∀ c : A ⊕ B → K, HasSum (fun μ ↦ c μ • adaptedFamily g A B μ) x →
          ∀ b : B, c (Sum.inr b) = 0
doc:
/-- **An orthonormal basis adapted to a submodule**: for every submodule `N` of `Tˢ` there are
generators `g j ∈ N` of norm one and an orthonormal basis of `Tˢ` consisting of multiples
`X^ν • g j` and monomial vectors, in which the elements of `N` are the series in the multiples
`X^ν • g j`. Source: Bosch 1.3/10 and the remark after 1.3/7 ("the system `(y_μ)_{μ ∈ M'}` is seen
to be an orthonormal basis of `𝔞`"). -/

name: exists_generators_forall_exists_isNearest
statement:
theorem exists_generators_forall_exists_isNearest (N : Submodule 𝕋 (ι → 𝕋)) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (g : Fin r → ι → 𝕋), (∀ j, g j ∈ N) ∧ (∀ j, ‖g j‖ = 1) ∧
      ∀ f : ι → 𝕋, ∃ q : Fin r → 𝕋, (∀ j, ‖q j‖ ≤ ‖f‖) ∧
        ∀ a ∈ N, ‖f - ∑ j, q j • g j‖ ≤ ‖f - ∑ j, q j • g j - a‖
doc:
/-- **Generators with a best approximation**: every submodule `N` of `Tˢ` has generators
`g₁, …, g_r` of norm one such that every `f ∈ Tˢ` has a combination `Σ qⱼ gⱼ` with `‖qⱼ‖ ≤ ‖f‖`
which is a nearest point of `N` to `f`. Source: Bosch 1.3/7, 1.3/9, 1.3/10. -/

name: exists_generators_norm_le
statement:
theorem exists_generators_norm_le (N : Submodule 𝕋 (ι → 𝕋)) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (g : Fin r → ι → 𝕋), (∀ j, g j ∈ N) ∧ (∀ j, ‖g j‖ = 1) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ N, ∃ q : Fin r → 𝕋, x = ∑ j, q j • g j ∧ ∀ j, ‖q j‖ ≤ ‖x‖
doc:
/-- Every submodule of `Tˢ` has generators `g₁, …, g_r` of norm one such that every element `x` of
it is `Σ qⱼ gⱼ` with `‖qⱼ‖ ≤ ‖x‖`. Source: Bosch 1.3/10; BGR 5.2.7/1 with the bound `ρ = 1`. -/

name: exists_forall_norm_sub_le
statement:
theorem exists_forall_norm_sub_le (N : Submodule 𝕋 (ι → 𝕋)) (f : ι → 𝕋) :
    ∃ a₀ ∈ N, ∀ a ∈ N, ‖f - a₀‖ ≤ ‖f - a‖
doc:
/-- **Submodules of `Tˢ` are strictly closed**: every `f` has a nearest point in the submodule.
Source: BGR 5.2.7/7; Bosch 1.3/9. -/

name: isClosed_submodule
statement: theorem isClosed_submodule (N : Submodule 𝕋 (ι → 𝕋)) : IsClosed (N : Set (ι → 𝕋))
doc: /-- Submodules of `Tˢ` are closed. Source: BGR 5.2.7/1; Bosch 1.3/8. -/

name: infDist_mem_range_norm
statement:
theorem infDist_mem_range_norm (N : Submodule 𝕋 (ι → 𝕋)) (f : ι → 𝕋) :
    Metric.infDist f (N : Set (ι → 𝕋)) ∈ Set.range (norm : K → ℝ)
doc:
/-- The distance of a point of `Tˢ` to a submodule is the norm of an element of `K`: the residue
norm on a finite `T`-module presented as `Tˢ ⧸ N` takes its values in `‖K‖`.
Source: BGR 5.2.7/8. -/

name: exists_generators_norm_le_ideal
statement:
theorem exists_generators_norm_le_ideal (I : Ideal 𝕋) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (g : Fin r → 𝕋), (∀ j, g j ∈ I) ∧ (∀ j, ‖g j‖ = 1) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ I, ∃ q : Fin r → 𝕋, x = ∑ j, q j * g j ∧ ∀ j, ‖q j‖ ≤ ‖x‖
doc:
/-- Every ideal of the Tate algebra has generators `a₁, …, a_r` of norm one such that every element
`f` of it is `Σ fᵢ aᵢ` with `‖fᵢ‖ ≤ ‖f‖`. Source: Bosch 1.3/7. -/

name: exists_forall_norm_sub_le_ideal
statement:
theorem exists_forall_norm_sub_le_ideal (I : Ideal 𝕋) (f : 𝕋) :
    ∃ a₀ ∈ I, ∀ a ∈ I, ‖f - a₀‖ ≤ ‖f - a‖
doc:
/-- **Ideals of the Tate algebra are strictly closed**: every series has a nearest point in the
ideal. Source: BGR 5.2.7/8; Bosch 1.3/9. -/

name: isClosed_ideal
statement: theorem isClosed_ideal (I : Ideal 𝕋) : IsClosed (I : Set 𝕋)
doc: /-- **Ideals of the Tate algebra are closed.** Source: BGR 5.2.7/2; Bosch 1.3/8. -/

name: norm_quotient_mk_mem_range_norm
statement:
theorem norm_quotient_mk_mem_range_norm (I : Ideal 𝕋) (f : 𝕋) :
    ‖Ideal.Quotient.mk I f‖ ∈ Set.range (norm : K → ℝ)
doc:
/-- The residue norm on a quotient of the Tate algebra takes its values in `‖K‖`:
`|Tₙ ⧸ 𝔞| = |K|`. Source: BGR 5.2.7/8. -/

name: Module.Dual.exists_bound_of_forall_exists_ne_zero
statement:
theorem Module.Dual.exists_bound_of_forall_exists_ne_zero {K : Type*} [NormedField K]
    {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (N : V → ℝ)
    (h : ∀ x : V, x ≠ 0 → ∃ φ : V →ₗ[K] K, (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ y, ‖φ y‖ ≤ C * N y) ∧ φ x ≠ 0)
    (ψ : V →ₗ[K] K) : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ y, ‖ψ y‖ ≤ C * N y
doc:
/-- On a finite-dimensional space, if the functionals bounded with respect to a function `N`
separate the points, then every functional is bounded with respect to `N`.
Source: BGR 2.3.1/2. -/

name: norm_trace_le_spectralNorm
statement: theorem norm_trace_le_spectralNorm (x : L) : ‖Algebra.trace K L x‖ ≤ spectralNorm K L x
doc:
/-- The trace of a finite extension is a contraction for the spectral norm.
Source: BGR 3.2.3/2. -/

name: exists_bound_of_isSeparable
statement:
theorem exists_bound_of_isSeparable [Algebra.IsSeparable K L] (φ : L →ₗ[K] K) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ y, ‖φ y‖ ≤ C * spectralNorm K L y
doc:
/-- **A finite separable extension is weakly cartesian for the spectral norm**: every linear
functional on it is bounded. Source: BGR 3.5.1/3. -/

name: isWeaklyStable_of_perfectField
statement:
theorem isWeaklyStable_of_perfectField (K : Type u) [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K]
    [PerfectField K] : IsWeaklyStable K
doc: /-- **Perfect fields are weakly stable.** Source: BGR 3.5.1/4. -/

name: isWeaklyStable_of_completeSpace
statement:
theorem isWeaklyStable_of_completeSpace (K : Type u) [NontriviallyNormedField K]
    [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] : IsWeaklyStable K
doc:
/-- **Complete fields are weakly stable.** Source: BGR 3.5.2 ("it follows from Proposition 2.3.3/4
that each complete field `K` is weakly stable"). -/

name: normAbsoluteValue
statement:
noncomputable def normAbsoluteValue (A : Type*) [NormedCommRing A] [NormMulClass A] [Nontrivial A]
    (Q : Type*) [Field Q] [Algebra A Q] [IsFractionRing A Q] : AbsoluteValue Q ℝ where
doc:
/-- The multiplicative extension of the norm of a normed domain to its fraction field:
`|a / b| = ‖a‖ / ‖b‖`. Source: BGR 3.5.3 ("`K` is the field of fractions of `A`, and the valuation
on `K` extends the valuation on `A`"), 1.5.3. -/

name: normAbsoluteValue_algebraMap
statement: theorem normAbsoluteValue_algebraMap (a : A) : normAbsoluteValue A Q (algebraMap A Q a) = ‖a‖

name: normAbsoluteValue_div
statement:
theorem normAbsoluteValue_div (a : A) {b : A} (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    normAbsoluteValue A Q (algebraMap A Q a / algebraMap A Q b) = ‖a‖ / ‖b‖

name: isNonarchimedean_normAbsoluteValue
statement:
theorem isNonarchimedean_normAbsoluteValue [IsUltrametricDist A] :
    IsNonarchimedean (normAbsoluteValue A Q)

name: isUltrametricDist
statement:
theorem isUltrametricDist [IsUltrametricDist A] :
    letI := normedField A Q
    IsUltrametricDist Q

name: isJapaneseRing_of_perfectField
statement:
theorem isJapaneseRing_of_perfectField (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A] [PerfectField (FractionRing A)] :
    IsJapaneseRing A
doc:
/-- **A noetherian integrally closed domain with perfect fraction field is Japanese.**
Source: BGR 4.3/2, from Dedekind's theorem 4.2/1. -/

name: isWeaklyStable_fractionRing
statement:
theorem isWeaklyStable_fractionRing (n : ℕ) :
    letI := IsFractionRing.normedField (TateAlgebra K n) (FractionRing (TateAlgebra K n))
    IsWeaklyStable (FractionRing (TateAlgebra K n))
doc:
/-- **The fraction field of the Tate algebra is weakly stable**, in characteristic zero.
Source: BGR 5.3.1/1 ("All valued fields of characteristic `0` are weakly stable"). -/

name: isJapaneseRing
statement: theorem isJapaneseRing (n : ℕ) : IsJapaneseRing (TateAlgebra K n)
doc:
/-- **The Tate algebra is Japanese**, in characteristic zero. Source: BGR 5.3.1/3 ("the assertion
follows from Proposition 4.3/2 if `char k = 0`"). -/

name: norm_X
statement: theorem norm_X (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) : ‖Restricted.X K (1 : Fin n → ℝ) i‖ = 1
doc: /-- The variables of the Tate algebra have Gauss norm one. -/

name: not_isMulDistinguishedX0_X_one
statement:
theorem not_isMulDistinguishedX0_X_one (s : ℕ) :
    ¬ IsMulDistinguishedX0 (Restricted.X K (1 : Fin 2 → ℝ) 1) s
doc: /-- The variable `X 1` of `T₂` is not `X 0`-distinguished of any order. -/

name: isMulDistinguishedX0_shear_X_one
statement:
theorem isMulDistinguishedX0_shear_X_one :
    IsMulDistinguishedX0 (shear K 1 (fun _ ↦ 1) (Restricted.X K (1 : Fin 2 → ℝ) 1)) 1
doc:
/-- After the shear `X 1 ↦ X 1 + X 0` the variable `X 1` of `T₂` is `X 0`-distinguished of
order one. -/

name: isMaximal_ker_aeval
statement:
theorem isMaximal_ker_aeval {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → K) (hx : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ 1) :
    (RingHom.ker (aeval (K := K) (1 : Fin n → ℝ) x hx)).IsMaximal
doc: /-- The kernel of the evaluation at a `K`-rational point of the unit ball is a maximal ideal. -/

name: norm_one_add_p_mul_X
statement:
theorem norm_one_add_p_mul_X :
    ‖(1 + Restricted.C (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) (p : ℚ_[p]) * Restricted.X ℚ_[p] (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) 0 :
      TateAlgebra ℚ_[p] 1)‖ = 1
doc: /-- The Gauss norm of `1 + p X` over `ℚ_[p]` is one. -/

name: isUnit_one_add_p_mul_X
statement:
theorem isUnit_one_add_p_mul_X :
    IsUnit (1 + Restricted.C (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) (p : ℚ_[p]) * Restricted.X ℚ_[p] (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) 0 :
      TateAlgebra ℚ_[p] 1)
doc: /-- The series `1 + p X` is a unit of `T₁` over `ℚ_[p]`. -/

name: reduction_p_add_X_add_p_mul_X_sq
statement:
theorem reduction_p_add_X_add_p_mul_X_sq
    (h : ‖(Restricted.C (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) (p : ℚ_[p]) + Restricted.X ℚ_[p] (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) 0 +
      Restricted.C (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) (p : ℚ_[p]) * Restricted.X ℚ_[p] (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) 0 ^ 2 :
        TateAlgebra ℚ_[p] 1)‖ ≤ 1) :
    reduction ⟨Restricted.C (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) (p : ℚ_[p]) + Restricted.X ℚ_[p] (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) 0 +
      Restricted.C (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) (p : ℚ_[p]) * Restricted.X ℚ_[p] (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) 0 ^ 2,
        mem_unitClosedBall.2 h⟩ = MvPolynomial.X 0
doc: /-- The reduction of `p + X + p X²` over `ℚ_[p]` is `X`. -/

name: isWeierstrassPolynomial_example
statement:
theorem isWeierstrassPolynomial_example :
    IsWeierstrassPolynomial ℚ_[p] 1
      (Polynomial.X ^ 2 - Polynomial.C (Restricted.C (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) (p : ℚ_[p]) *
        Restricted.X ℚ_[p] (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) 0) * Polynomial.X -
          Polynomial.C (Restricted.C (1 : Fin 1 → ℝ) (p : ℚ_[p])))
doc: /-- The polynomial `X² - p X₁ X - p` over `T₁ = ℚ_[p]⟨X₁⟩` is a Weierstrass polynomial. -/

name: isMaximal_span_X_sq_sub_p
statement:
theorem isMaximal_span_X_sq_sub_p :
    (Ideal.span {ofPolynomial ℚ_[p] 0
      (Polynomial.X ^ 2 - Polynomial.C (Restricted.C (1 : Fin 0 → ℝ) (p : ℚ_[p])))}).IsMaximal
doc:
/-- The ideal `(X² - p)` of `T₁` over `ℚ_[p]` is maximal, with residue field the quadratic
extension `ℚ_[p](√p)`. -/
